hardening: linearity-runner-clock is matched per job, by any one line of the failed-step log (ci-rerun.sh:242-247), and the unit-test step prints every shard's output in one log (test.yaml:507-524, unittest-shards.py:189-191), so a `test (` job that fails a linearity test and a real test together is rerun once as this flake and recorded in ci-reruns.tsv under its id. A deterministic failure stays red; a nondeterministic real failure gets a second attempt and is misattributed. The registry test checks each sample and each REAL_FAILURES line alone (test_ci_rerun.py:93-103, :634-647), never a log holding both. Smallest hardening: for a signature of named tests, require every `FAIL:` and `ERROR:` line of the log to match its log_regex before the job counts as a flake, and add a REAL_FAILURES sample that holds a linearity FAIL line beside a real one.

The report test's growth bound now sits 1.2x below the quadratic growth it guards (12 against the measured 14.7x per 4x step, test_validate_agent_assets.py:2705-2707), and with the new signature its first failure is rerun once, so a superlinear regression milder than the measured one passes, and one near it gets two draws. Judging the larger step 32,000 to 128,000 (quadratic 16x against linear 4x) or counting the scan's line-feed passes instead of wall time would keep the guard independent of the runner's clock.
